title: El mandado
goal: Earn your first córdobas carrying somebody else’s shopping
culture: The mirror of the cargador in the market: there you paid, and agreeing the price first was the etiquette. Here you are the one carrying, and letting her name the figure is the move — the work is small and she is a neighbour.

beats.es: (Va cargada con cuatro bolsas y le falta media cuadra.)
beats.en: I’ll carry it for you, doña.
beats.good: The same sentence the porter used on you in the market, now coming out of your mouth. That is the whole arc of this district in one line.

beats.es: ¡Ay, sí, mi hijo! ¿Y cuánto me cobra?
beats.good: ¿Cuánto me da? lets her set it, which is right when the work is small and the person is a neighbour. ¿Cuánto me cobra? was for when you were the one buying.
Twenty córdobas for three blocks. It is not much and it is the first money you have earned in Spanish, which is a different thing.

beats.es: Gracias, mi hijo. Cuando quiera, ahí me busca.
beats.good: Cuando quiera — whenever you like. It is an offer of more work, and the correct answer is the same two words straight back.
